Honestly, Dead Rising 1 is a fun game, especially once you learn the ins and outs, level up properly and replay the game on said leveled up save file...

But god, I would not recommend you play this game under most circumstances.

As fun as the game can be at times, it has not aged the best, especially in comparison to the sequels (Primarily Dead Rising 2).
Obvious issues like the survivor AI being terrible and the pathfinding being genuine garbage make this way more unenjoyable than it has to be.
The game is far too easy to cheese pretty early on, which is honestly necessary with how horrid the AI is.
Otis is the single most annoying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ possible.
The constant stunning and tossing around is a pain in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ass. Get caught with your pants down and you go from max to no health because of 1 cultist.
The wait during the final mission during 72 hour mode is filled with bulletspongy enemies that are complete pushovers and yet somehow annoying to deal with, so unless you really slowly wanna farm PP, you better wait for a LONG while.
All of this combined makes it feel like there's never enough time for ANYTHING, purely because of how much everything and everyone drags you down.

Outside of that, the character, charm and atmosphere is great.
The weapon variety is fun, ranging from pointless garbage like the water gun to funny and effective stuff like the bowling ball to straight up broken like the small chainsaw. You see it? You can probably use it to beat a zombie to death.
The fact levels stay between same save playthroughs is a nice incentive to keep replaying the game over and over.
The characters and story are (mostly) great, and so are the psychopaths and their fights (again, mostly).

Why wouldn't I recommend it though?

Dead Rising 2 exists.

Nearly everything bad about DR1 is fixed in DR2 and nearly everything good in DR1 is expanded upon in DR2.
If you can somehow manage to run DR2 without crashing, it's a WAY more enjoyable experience than DR1 by a long shot.
Combo weapons added much needed weapon variety to the game, the map is much more expansive and there's far more to do.

I'd play DR1 for the nostalgia or to experience how the series started off, but I'd recommend you try DR2 first.

As for the other games, OTR is sort of a directors cut for DR2 (though I prefer vanilla DR2), DR3 is honestly not as bad as many people say and DR4 is a horrible Dead Rising game with a horrible story but can be fun if you just block out any memory of the fact it's a DR game.

i used to love this game as a child, but replaying this as an adult has been one of the most frustrating gaming experiences I have ever had. The game feels brutal not because of well designed game mechanics like other games that are difficult, but due to horrible AI, bad design choices, and things that are straight up unfair to new/returning players. The AI is horrific, and half the game is based on you escorting AI.... They get stuck on zombies extremely easily, stop in place for no reason, and you essentially have to babysit them the entire way back to the safe room. This process is not only ball-busting but just not fun in the slightest it makes me wonder who the hell thought half the game should be you doing this over and over. The bosses are designed like ♥♥♥♥ and are extremely unfun in pretty much every way. They do a ton of damage, have horrible AI just like the people you rescue, and lack any sort of actual fun gameplay. 75% of the boss fights that I have played through so far is the AI tweaking out for no reason, and the best way to beat it is to sit in a corner and spam 100 pistol shots into their face before they die. My last issue with this game are the constant knowledge checks. For example, why are there boss encounters that happen without any prior warning? One of my first deaths coming back was unknowingly walking into a boss encounter with barely any health and no proper weapon. On top of that, even when there IS a boss fight that you know is coming, a ton of the bosses need a gun to be possible at all, yet the game only gives you a gun the first fight in the game. So you better have guessed that you needed to walk into the fight with a pistol or youre ♥♥♥♥♥♥. The time limit makes this issue 10x worse because not only are you fighting constant knowledge checks but you also are under a time limit while trying to figure out what youre supposed to do. There are several side missions where I had no idea what the game wanted me to do and I had to google them, such as the person you are supposed to hit a couple times to get them to come with you. The first time I did that side mission the melee weapon I had killed him instantly so I had no idea you could even pacify him. It feels like half the game is a mix of these weird knowledge checks that make it miserable to play coming back. I do have fond memories of this game, but in 2026 this is just not a good game sorry to say. I really wouldn't recommend it to anyone that isn't already a fan of the series.

Dead Rising is a very unique zombie game and is a lot of fun but it has it's flaws for sure. Now, I played this game for the first time couple of years ago so I never got to truly experience the game at release. I could imagine it would be super revolutionary for it's time, but it's hard to not notice some flaws today. The aiming is horrible, the survivor ai is also horrible and I'm torn on the time mechanic. On one hand it's super cool but it's soooo punishing.  Essentially if you miss the timing for a missing that mission is gone for your whole playthrough so either load a previous save or just lose that mission. Also there is some other jank from the game being pretty old which is to be expected.

Now as I said this is a very unique zombie game taking inspiration from George A. Romero's Dawn of the Dead which takes place in a mall and therefore kind of spinning the genre on it's head. A lot of zombie games at Dead Rising's release were pretty focused on shooting and having firepower. Dead Rising however focuses on using more boring items most often which is AWESOME. Instead of relying exclusively on guns and explosives, expect to find buckets, skateboards, baseball bats, garden shears, lawnmowers, etc. You can get guns and things like that but most of the time you use random things as weapons and the best weapons generally are melee weapons. 

Also the psychopath battles are genuinely some of the best bosses I've ever seen. The fights themselves are pretty good, but the cutscenes are phenomenal. Overall i think the story is pretty great an the characters are all really memorable and great (except you Otis, I hate you). You also get ablities which kind of gives you the power-fantasy of being Steve Austin in a zombie apocalypse and it's a lot of fun too, but I will say the earlier levels are pretty rough and it takes a while to get to max lvl. Overall, i would recommend this game to most people, if you're willing to overlook a few issues. This is the most "Dead Rising" Dead Rising game if that makes sense. DR2 Off The Record and DR3 are also good but feel very different so if you want kind of the pure DR experience, then play DR1.

Dead Rising is one-of-the-kind zombie apocalypse + sandbox without hardcore element. Don't ask me about Project Zomboid or DayZ, cuz that is purely survive or die instead something fun and potentially goofy without worrying yourself starving to death. 

[h3]Obvious bias[/h3]
I love how almost everything in the game is interactable, like you can pick up and use it, or throw it like no tomorrow. And of course, certain items like food can be cook or mix to get power up consumable instead solely as a joke weapon or healing item.

Not to mention, there is leveling system. Player can either get the best photographically impressive shot to score higher, or kill zombies, or rescue civillians. Level up including more move sets (e.g. jumping on top of hordes of zombies) to health increase or even additional item slot. Some move set can be a bit gimmicky, but it at least it actually provides viable way to deal with threat rather than mindlessly killing.

[h3]The dated[/h3]
This game takes me back to old GTA era, where player must manually save the game via in-world location. Except this game intentionally punishes you for good and bad reason; Good thing is that your player stats upon death can be retain and pass onto next run. Bad thing is that you have to go through the entire game again. (Actually that doesn't sounds too bad if player wanted to try out different things in other runs without leveling up again, but Im just used to full playthrough)

The stagger/stun soft-lock when getting damage. You pray the enemy doesn't have automatic firearm or rapid attacks, as you feel extremely vulnerable (in an NPC way). Whether its good or not is also subjective.

[h3]Overall[/h3]
Hands down the best "sandbox" category game in zombie apocalypse (which stated in the beginning), something you hardly able to find in a more serious/hardcore genre.

I dont usually speak for big titles because i like to raise the voice in the more lesser known games, but to this day i still find people that dont know about this game's existence, but heres my words or word..

[b] PEAK.. [/b]

Thats all i have to say. One of the Classic Zombie Titles back in the early 2000s, the Xbox 360 era. I remember i played the 2nd one, Dead Rising 2, before playing the first game, If you wanna delve into one of the most legendary zombie titles, Dead Rising is one worthy to pick up, This was made by CAPCOM, same people that made Resident Evil, so you know they cooked. Unfortunately Dead Rising didnt catch into the spotlight more often than its more successful titles, the franchise was certainly behind the curtains for the more niche audience.

'Original' is gonna be the big word for this entry specifically, for all the Zombie followers out there, this is the big dream scenario of 'A Zombie Apocalypse just started and you're trapped in a Shopping Mall' everything is at your disposal, walk into any store and start picking and wearing everything you find. I remember the game really expressed itself on using EVERYTHING as a weapon, you can pick up an entire Park Bench and swing it around as a weapon, Zombies in this game are expendable, they are easy to kill but they are always the persistent threat throughout the entire game as you explore and follow the narrative of the story.

Of course throughout the game, you level up, unlock new skill moves, increase in stats via Health, Damage and Speed, this make making a path to your next goal more easier, making it trivial to survive against the undead, but then comes Psychopath encounters, human bosses that can potentially one shot you even in the beginning of the game and be sure to save often! Because theres no Auto-save in this original, the game will always keep throwing more and more new threats.

Dead Rising has neeever been known for its difficulty however, it has a very laid back playstyle, a 'do whatever you want' playground freedom.. although just make sure not to miss your main story missions, the time scope can be reaaaallly tight if you're not carefully spending your minutes escorting a survivor allll the way back to the safehouse.

The port here itself is good! I'd stamp it with approval, a recommendation I would say.. Perhaps use a controller?... That is if you wanna pull off all the tricky skill moves Frank unlocks down the line, or you can master the art of keyboard controls, its possible, but be warned some of them have some realllly wonky activations if i recalled, and its like a milisecond of pressing two keys at the same time.

Don't sleep on this one because of the generic zombie name, like I did. This is a wonderfully cheesy, flawed and, above all, a charming game. The premise is that you're locked in a mall with zombies for 72 hours (one in-game minute = 5 actual seconds) and you can use anything found in the mall as a weapon against the hordes, while completing missions. It's enormously fun to weaponize benches, potted plants, mannequins, TVs, power tools, bowling balls, plywood panels, lawn mowers and whatever else you can find. I also the realized how much I like X360/PS3-era graphics - somewhat realistic, yet videogamey and very clean and readable.
